header.title: Create VM: Other NAS Systems
header.description: ProxMenux can create a ready-to-install VM for TrueNAS SCALE, TrueNAS CORE, OpenMediaVault, XigmaNAS, Rockstor, ZimaOS and FygoOS. This page covers the shared creation flow (default / advanced configuration, the new storage plan, optional GPU passthrough) plus per-system notes and recommended specs.

intro.title: How these systems are created
intro.bodyRich: All seven systems share the same ProxMenux wizard. The NAS selector picks the matching installer (auto-detecting the latest stable version for TrueNAS, OMV, XigmaNAS, Rockstor and FygoOS) and then hands over to the generic VM configurator and the storage plan. ZimaOS uses its own installer script (vm/zimaos.sh) but follows the same CPU / RAM / storage / optional-GPU sequence.

config.heading: Default vs Advanced configuration
config.intro: When a NAS is selected, ProxMenux asks whether to use the default VM profile or open the advanced wizard. The defaults are tuned for NAS workloads — more RAM than a plain Linux VM because ZFS-based systems need it for the ARC cache.
config.advancedIntro: The advanced wizard exposes every parameter individually:

advancedRowsRich.optionsRich: Host, KVM64 and other listed CPU models

config.zfsCalloutBody: TrueNAS SCALE / CORE and XigmaNAS use ZFS, whose ARC cache benefits from RAM. TrueNAS needs at least 8 GB for basic use; 16 GB or more can help with heavier services and apps. Size the VM for the chosen distribution and workload rather than treating 8 GB as a universal ZFS minimum. Lighter OMV, Rockstor or ZimaOS setups can need less.

storagePlan.heading: Storage plan
storagePlan.intro: After CPU / RAM, ProxMenux opens the Storage Plan menu, where you can combine virtual disks, imported disks and PCI passthrough devices in the same VM, adding items one at a time and finishing when you are done.
virtualItemsRich: Lists the Proxmox storage volumes available on the host.
You pick the target storage and the size in GB.
The disk uses the selected bus: SCSI (default), SATA, VirtIO or IDE. SATA slots are sata0, sata1, …, with six slots numbered 0–5.
importItemsRich: Detects physical disks that are safe to import (system and protected disks are hidden).
You select one or more disks via a checklist.
Imported disks use the selected bus and are attached via qm set.
storagePlan.pciHeading: c. Add Controller or NVMe (PCI passthrough)
pciItemsRich: Detects SATA/SAS HBAs and NVMe devices on the host and lets you pass an entire controller into the VM. IOMMU must be enabled; the script offers to enable it and reboots if required.
A confirmation step warns about controller-wide risk (the whole card, including every disk on it, leaves the host).

The selected PCI devices are attached with commands such as qm set VMID --hostpci0 PCI_ADDRESS,pcie=1. Replace VMID and PCI_ADDRESS with the VM ID and PCI address, and use an unused hostpci index for each device.
storagePlan.resetCalloutBodyRich: The menu also offers r (reset the current selection and start over) and d (finish and continue). You cannot finish with an empty plan.

gpu.heading: Optional GPU passthrough
gpu.bodyRich: After the storage plan, if a compatible GPU is detected on the host, ProxMenux offers to launch the GPU passthrough assistant. See <link>Add GPU to a VM (Passthrough)</link> for how the assistant works — a host reboot may be required.

autoFeatures.heading: Automatic VM features
autoFeatures.efiBody: When OVMF (UEFI) is selected, ProxMenux automatically creates a 4 MB EFI disk on the storage you pick, formatted to match the storage type (raw for directory-based storage).
autoFeatures.isoBodyRich: The installation ISO is downloaded (if needed) and attached to ide2 as a CD-ROM, ready for first boot.
autoFeatures.guestBody: The guest agent channel is enabled in the VM config. You still need to install the agent inside the guest after the NAS OS is up.

endToEnd.heading: What the script does end-to-end
itemsRich: Detects and downloads the latest stable ISO (or uses the fallback version if the upstream is unreachable).
Applies the default or advanced CPU / RAM / BIOS / machine type.
Opens the storage plan and attaches the selected virtual disks, imported disks and PCI devices.
Creates an EFI disk if UEFI is selected.
Sets the boot order (disk first, then ISO).
Enables the QEMU Guest Agent channel.
Optionally runs the GPU passthrough assistant.
Generates a styled HTML description attached to the VM.
Starts the VM if you chose to.

truenasScale.title: TrueNAS SCALE
truenasScale.description: Debian-based TrueNAS with Docker apps in current releases, Linux KVM and ZFS as the primary filesystem. Older SCALE releases used Kubernetes. It combines ZFS storage with a container ecosystem.
specs: Recommended interface: SATA or SCSI (both support discard/trim)
Minimum RAM: 8 GB (16 GB+ recommended for real workloads)
VirtIO network adapter for best throughput

truenasCore.title: TrueNAS CORE
truenasCore.description: FreeBSD-based TrueNAS, formerly FreeNAS, focused on ZFS storage. CORE 13.3 jails, plugins and virtualization features are obsolete and unsupported; current development focuses on the Linux-based editions.
specs: VirtIO network adapter for best throughput

openmediavault.title: OpenMediaVault
openmediavault.description: Debian-based NAS with a modular plugin system. Light on resources and easy to run on modest hardware — a natural choice when you do not need ZFS.
specs: BIOS: ProxMenux defaults to SeaBIOS for OMV (override in Advanced if needed)
VirtIO network adapter for best throughput

xigmanas.title: XigmaNAS
xigmanas.description: FreeBSD-based NAS — the direct continuation of the original FreeNAS (0.7) codebase. Focused on ZFS and simplicity, with a lighter footprint than TrueNAS.
specs: Minimum RAM: 4 GB (8 GB+ recommended for ZFS)
VirtIO network adapter for best throughput

rockstor.title: Rockstor
rockstor.description: openSUSE Leap-based NAS built around Btrfs. Snapshots, subvolumes and the Rock-ons app framework (Docker) for media, file sharing and backup.
specs: VirtIO network adapter for best throughput

zimaos.title: ZimaOS
zimaos.description: Lightweight NAS / home-server OS built with Buildroot, evolved from CasaOS, with a focus on media, Docker apps and home automation. ZimaOS uses a dedicated ProxMenux installer (vm/zimaos.sh) that downloads a pre-built image, while offering CPU, RAM and storage configuration.
specs: Default RAM: 4 GB (enough for media / self-hosted apps)
VirtIO network adapter for best throughput

fygoos.title: FygoOS
fygoos.description: International edition of fnOS, a Debian-based NAS. ProxMenux downloads the latest installer ISO published on fygonas.com and mounts it in the VM. The installer puts the system on one disk; the space left on that disk can hold volumes for apps and files. After the installation, the console shows the address of the web interface, on port 5666 (port 80 redirects to it): open it in a browser to name the device and create the administrator account.
specs: System disk: FygoOS proposes a 64 GB system partition, which can be smaller in a VM
Installation: Graphical Install, or Rescuing Install if the graphical one fails
UEFI (OVMF) boot without Secure Boot keys, as the installer requires
Network: Ethernet with DHCP by default
VirtIO network adapter for best throughput
